observations: The original different-package cancellation case passed its warm interactions in one application PID20215.
Delta Apps was tapped at118.76s, its title-based window query disappeared at120.28s, a global catalog button existed at121.57s, and app termination began at121.63s.
The next actual cold process restored delta with Result saved. Its saved sceneValue and presentedSceneValue both still contained its UUID.
Gamma had a persisted null presentedSceneValue while its original sceneValue remained the gamma UUID.
The later failed alpha case cleanup tapped Apps at49.14s and terminated at50.78s. The next cold process restored alpha as Cancelled.
All four scene sessions remained in KnownSceneSessions. Setting the request binding to nil had not destroyed those native scenes.
inference: The last UI change did not reach the saved presentation value before process termination. This is consistent with deferred state restoration persistence; it is not proof of an Apple framework defect.
implementation: Keep the original UUID-valued miniapp-invocation WindowGroup.
Give the root WindowGroup a Codable/Hashable catalog-or-request identity so a pending request in a reused root is not mistaken for an available catalog.
On Apps from a multiwindow request, open/focus the catalog value and dismiss the current native scene through SwiftUI dismissWindow().
Use the existing request binding for single-window platforms. Do not delete requests, attachments, prepared results, or another window.
